episode.title: Remove an ineligible model from the generated built-in catalog
episode.before: At parent commit 6aedd1066e540642165aa30fa7b4a1b863778aa7, grok-build-0.1 was not in the xAI exclusion set. Consequently, when upstream discovery returned it as tool-capable, the common catalog filter allowed it into generated provider data. The provider test treated the entry as present and asserted its supported thinking levels.
episode.after: At commit 0dbf2b76fe7919d5fe4184523898507b4ae19ee0, grok-build-0.1 is in the xAI exclusion set, so the generator removes it before metadata enrichment, grouping, and catalog serialization. The provider test now requires the ID to be absent and no longer dereferences it for capability assertions.
episode.diff: The implementation adds grok-build-0.1 to XAI_BUILTIN_EXCLUDED_MODEL_IDS. The test adds that ID to the retired/redundant-model absence cases and removes its thinking-level assertion. A nearby comment is generalized because the removed entry is no longer an applicable example. No runtime provider or generated shard source was directly edited.

evidence_units.claim: The pinned implementation commit is 0dbf2b76fe7919d5fe4184523898507b4ae19ee0 with parent 6aedd1066e540642165aa30fa7b4a1b863778aa7; its subject states that Grok Build 0.1 is removed from the built-in catalog.
evidence_units.source: git show --format=fuller 0dbf2b76fe7919d5fe4184523898507b4ae19ee0; issue-bundle.json resolved_commit and parent_commit

evidence_units.claim: The parent exclusion set omitted grok-build-0.1.
The pinned implementation adds grok-build-0.1 to the set of model IDs excluded from the built-in xAI catalog.
Discovered tool-capable xAI models are initially converted into openai-responses catalog candidates before the common filtering stage.
The common catalog filter rejects an xAI candidate when its ID belongs to XAI_BUILTIN_EXCLUDED_MODEL_IDS; therefore the new set member is removed before later metadata processing and serialization.
Generated xAI provider data is flattened into XAI_MODELS, and the runtime provider exposes Object.values(XAI_MODELS) as its selectable models.
Before the change, the catalog test did not require grok-build-0.1 to be absent and instead dereferenced it to assert low, medium, and high thinking levels.
After the change, the catalog test includes grok-build-0.1 among IDs that must not occur in XAI_MODELS and removes its thinking-level assertion while retaining capability checks for admitted entries.
The change modifies only the generator source and its provider-specific test: four inserted lines and three deleted lines across two files.

The repository contains a direct regression oracle: Object.keys(XAI_MODELS) must not contain the excluded ID. The available evidence does not record execution results for that test at the pinned commit.
evidence_units.source: git show 0dbf2b76fe7919d5fe4184523898507b4ae19ee0:packages/ai/test/xai-responses.test.ts lines 115-125; issue-bundle.json metadata_unavailable and verification fields

candidate_atomics.name: exclude-ineligible-discovered-model
candidate_atomics.title: Exclude an ineligible discovered model from the built-in catalog
candidate_atomics.description: Add a model identifier to the provider-scoped exclusion contract so upstream discovery can still ingest it, but catalog generation removes it before enrichment and serialization.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent a retired, redundant, or otherwise ineligible upstream-discovered model from being offered through the built-in runtime catalog.
semantic_action.pre_state: The upstream discovery source may return a tool-capable model whose provider and identifier pass the existing catalog filter, allowing it to reach generated provider data and runtime selection.
semantic_action.post_state: A candidate matching the configured provider and excluded identifier is removed before metadata enrichment, provider grouping, serialization, and runtime exposure.
semantic_action.validation: Generate or hydrate the catalog and assert that the provider catalog's keys do not contain the excluded identifier.

candidate_atomics.name: reconcile-capability-tests-with-catalog-membership
candidate_atomics.title: Reconcile capability tests with catalog membership
candidate_atomics.description: Change the catalog contract test from asserting metadata on the removed entry to asserting that the entry is absent, while preserving capability checks for admitted entries.

semantic_action.intent: Make the regression oracle enforce catalog membership policy without dereferencing capability metadata for an entry that must no longer exist.
semantic_action.pre_state: The test suite assumes the ineligible model is present and validates its capabilities; the absence test does not name it.
semantic_action.post_state: The absence test names the excluded model, and capability assertions address only entries that remain admitted to the catalog.
semantic_action.validation: Run the provider-specific test and require both the excluded-key assertion and retained admitted-model capability assertions to pass.

candidate_workflows.name: remove-ineligible-model-from-generated-catalog
candidate_workflows.title: Remove an ineligible model from a generated built-in catalog
candidate_workflows.description: Apply a narrow provider-and-ID exclusion at the generator boundary, then reconcile membership and capability tests so generated and runtime catalogs cannot reintroduce or dereference the removed entry.

workflow_graph.goal: Ensure an upstream-discovered but ineligible model is absent from the built-in generated catalog and from the runtime provider's selectable model list.
when_to_use: An upstream catalog still reports a model that product policy classifies as retired, redundant, or unsuitable for the built-in catalog.
The repository generates provider catalogs from upstream metadata and already has a provider-scoped exclusion boundary.
Tests or call sites currently treat the model as a built-in catalog member.
anti_goals: Do not edit generated catalog shards directly when the generator is the source of truth.
Do not remove the provider, change request routing, or alter capabilities of unrelated admitted models.
Do not suppress all models from the upstream provider when only one identifier is ineligible.
Do not retain capability assertions for a model whose required invariant is absence.
not_applicable_when: The model must remain selectable and only its capability metadata is incorrect.
The catalog is maintained manually and has no generation or hydration boundary.
There is no direct implementation evidence establishing that the model reaches the built-in catalog.
The desired change concerns a user-supplied custom model rather than built-in catalog membership.
inputs: Provider identity whose generated catalog is affected
Exact upstream model identifier to exclude
Generated provider catalog consumed by runtime code
Provider-specific catalog membership and capability tests
workflow_graph.entry_state: Upstream discovery can produce the target model, the generator admits it, the runtime provider consumes the generated catalog, and tests assume the entry exists or fail to require its absence.
workflow_graph.exit_state: The generator rejects the provider-and-ID candidate before serialization, the runtime catalog cannot expose it after regeneration, and tests enforce absence without capability assertions for the removed entry.

steps.condition: The target identifier is confirmed to be ineligible for the built-in catalog while upstream discovery may still return it.
steps.validation: Trace the candidate from upstream ingestion through the exclusion predicate and confirm the predicate rejects the exact provider-and-ID pair before grouping and serialization.

steps.condition: Existing tests enumerate excluded entries or dereference the target entry's capability metadata.
steps.validation: The provider-specific test requires the target key to be absent and retains capability assertions only for admitted models.

validation_ladder: Inspect the parent state to prove the identifier was not excluded and was treated as a catalog member.
Inspect the generator path to prove upstream candidates pass through the provider-scoped exclusion predicate before serialization.
Assert the generated provider catalog does not contain the excluded identifier.
Assert retained built-in entries still have their expected routing and capability metadata.
Run the provider-specific regression test; run broader repository checks only when required by the repository's validation policy.
stop_conditions: Stop if the pinned change does not modify an implementation-bearing catalog boundary.
Stop if the target model is intended to remain selectable and only metadata needs correction.
Stop if no generated or runtime catalog call site can be traced from the changed filter.
Defer completion if catalog hydration or the provider-specific test cannot establish the absence invariant.
unresolved_or_deferred: The issue bundle lacks the PR body, review discussion, status checks, and recorded test execution results.

Generated provider data is ignored and absent from the pinned Git tree, so the serialized after-state cannot be inspected directly; it is established through the generator predicate, generated-catalog call sites, and regression oracle.
The repository evidence does not state the external product-policy reason that grok-build-0.1 was classified as retired or redundant.

unresolved_questions: Was the provider-specific test executed successfully at the pinned commit? The supplied bundle records the changed test but no status checks or command output.
What external lifecycle or product-policy evidence classified grok-build-0.1 as ineligible? The local implementation and commit establish the exclusion decision but not its upstream rationale.
